title: The gate reads an unreadable state file as empty, which fails open
description:
Filed from the Stage 1 review of opum-ai/test-skills#33 (TS-24, DEC-195 (7)(a)), verdict minor 2, quoted verbatim: "test_gate_matrix.py:56-59 locks in fail-open behaviour: a corrupt quarantine file means zero violations. That is arguably a product defect, since a corrupt state file silently passes the gate. If the fail-open is intended, fine. If not, the test cements it. This is worth a TS note, not a block."

The behaviour: _load_list and _load_list_text swallow ValueError and return [], so an unreadable .test-quarantine.json, .test-probation.json or baseline file reads as empty rather than as something the gate names.

This task does NOT decide whether fail-open is intended. That is the first thing it must settle, and if the answer is not derivable from the code or an existing decision it goes to opum-doc through the leader. Whichever way it is settled, the assertion at test_gate_matrix.py:56-59 must state the decision: if fail-open is intended, it stays and should say why; if not, it is inverted to expect a named failure.

Not started, and no code changed by filing it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The intended behaviour for an unreadable state file is decided and recorded in this task, with the reason, rather than assumed.
test_gate_matrix.py:56-59 asserts the decided behaviour: a named failure if fail-open is not intended, and the intended-reading with its reason if it is.

plan: 1. Cut fix/TS-30-fail-closed-unreadable-state-file off origin/dev and claim TS-30.
2. Replace the two swallowing loaders in gate.py with one that raises a named error carrying file, kind and parse error; tell missing from empty at the base ref with git ls-tree.
3. Convert that error into a named violation inside run() so the gate fails closed with a reason rather than crashing or passing.
4. Invert test_gate_matrix.py:56-59 and prove both directions in the same test: valid files pass, and an unparseable file of each kind fails by name.
5. Prove the mutation that restores the swallow turns the test red, with __pycache__ cleared on both arms.
6. Run the suite and the repo gate locally, open the PR, take a Stage 1 review, report.
implementationNotes: DECISION, recorded before the edit (AC0): FAIL CLOSED, ruled by opum-doc as DEC-213 on 2026-10-20T13:11:40Z and relayed by the leader, whose five terms are verbatim in the second implementation note on TS-32. An unparseable quarantine or probation file is a named violation and never passes; a MISSING file keeps its current meaning of no entries, so a fresh repository is not broken. Reason: the gate exists to stop a PR hiding tests from its own run, and a file the gate cannot parse is a state it cannot read, so reading it as empty is the one reading that always permits the action the gate exists to refuse. The baseline loader is not in this set: it already raises, which is what DEC-209 decided in words. No new test cases are added — the assertions go inside the existing parametrized test, so the test count and the baseline stay 95.

MEASURED, 2026-10-20, on branch fix/TS-30-fail-closed-unreadable-state-file at 25de32e (before review). Implementation: one StateFileError carrying file, kind and parse error, raised by both loaders; run() turns it into a single named violation (rule unreadable_state_file, Art. XI for quarantine, Art. XII for probation) and keeps running so the rest of the gate still reports. Presence at the base ref is asked with git ls-tree before content is read, because git show alone returns empty text for both a missing file and an existing empty one, and under term 3 an existing empty file is a parse failure rather than an absence. A missing file still returns no entries at head and at base.

EVIDENCE. Full PR-tier suite: 95 passed, 8 deselected — same count as the baseline, so no slot was spent and no test id moved. Repo gate run the way CI runs it (python skills/test-audit/scripts/tmx.py gate --policy test-policy.toml --junit report.xml --base origin/dev): PASS, rigor R4 Strict (the critical tier, because this diff touches gate.py), baseline_measured 95, growth 0, new_quarantine 0, new_probation 0. The term-3 control is inside the same test: before the corrupt file is written, a run with both files valid but probation absent asserts zero violations.

MUTATION PROOF, both arms with skills/test-audit/scripts/__pycache__ cleared: restoring the swallow in both loaders (except ValueError: return []) turns test_quarantine_windows red — 4 failed, the assertion reading [] == [unreadable_state_file] at the quarantine block; restoring the fixed file and clearing the cache turns it green — 4 passed. Re-run after the test shape changed below, same result.

FIXED MIDWAY, worth knowing: the first draft proved both kinds with a for loop in the test body, and the gate at R4 flagged smell conditional-logic (control flow around an assertion). The two kinds are now proved by two explicit blocks with no control flow, 6 assertions in the test, under the roulette threshold of 8.

NOT FIXED, outside the scope DEC-213 set and reported to the leader: the base-branch triage loader in run() still swallows ValueError to {} in the same shape; DEC-213 names only the quarantine and probation files.

BASE-REF PROBE, 2026-10-20, run in a disposable temp repo after the PR went green, to test the one claim the unit test cannot reach: presence at the base ref. Three fresh git repos, each with a valid empty quarantine file at head, run through gate.run with base=HEAD: base file MISSING -> no violations; base file EMPTY -> exactly one violation, unreadable_state_file; base file valid [] -> no violations. So the git ls-tree presence probe does distinguish an absent file from an existing unparseable one, which is term 3 exactly. Not added as a test: a base-ref git fixture would be a new case, and the slot rule sends that to the leader first. The probe script stayed in the session scratchpad and is not in the repo.
finalSummary:
The gate now fails closed on a state file it cannot parse (DEC-213, option A). gate.py: one StateFileError carrying file, kind and parse error, raised by the quarantine and probation loaders at head and at the base ref; run() turns it into a single named violation naming all three and continues, so a corrupt file is a reason rather than an empty list. A missing file still reads as no entries, and presence at the base ref is asked with git ls-tree so an existing empty file counts as a parse failure. tests/test_gate_matrix.py: the assertion that cemented the swallow is inverted in place and proves both directions — valid files pass, and an unparseable file of each kind fails by name. No new test cases and no slot: the PR-tier suite ran 95 passed and the baseline is unchanged at 95. Local gate in the CI shape: PASS at R4 Strict, baseline_measured 95, growth 0. Mutation proof: restoring the swallow turns the test red (4 failed); restored, it is green (4 passed), with __pycache__ cleared on both arms. Stage 1 review follows on the PR; extend this summary if it changes anything.

Also probed outside the suite, in a disposable repo: with the base ref holding a missing, an empty, and a valid empty quarantine file, the gate reports no violations, one unreadable_state_file, and none respectively.
